scenes.line1: How do Kafka producers keep data safe?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how Kafka producers keep your data consistent and ordered, even when things go wrong?

scenes.label: Key
scenes.sub: A key decides which partition gets your record.
scenes.say: When you set a key, Kafka uses it to pick a partition. That keeps all events for the same key in order.
The acks setting controls how safe your data is. Zero means no guarantee, one is leader only, and all is strongest.

scenes.label: Idempotent
scenes.sub: Avoids duplicates on retries since version 0.11.
scenes.say: Idempotent producers make sure retries never create duplicate records. That's a must for exactly-once delivery.

scenes.question: How does Kafka guarantee ordering?
scenes.wrong: Kafka keeps all messages in order.
scenes.right: Kafka only guarantees ordering within a partition. Use keys to keep related events together.
scenes.say: Here's a common interview trap: Kafka doesn't keep all messages in order, only within each partition. Use keys to group related events.
